Well, everyone left. At least I can take in the washing.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_310: How will my kids get home for supper?
You bricked up my door? I have bread in the oven!
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_311: Oh, poor thing! Needs a plantain leaf on that.
I always say: watch where you're going!
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_312: His poor wife... I'll take her a pie.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_313: Porridge would cook in no time on a fire like that.
Strange fire. That will make my milk go sour.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_314: Get that away from my house, right now!
A red box? I know boxes like that.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_315: Green blobs everywhere again. Who's cleaning that up?
Children, don't touch those little balls, they're hot!
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_316: Whose little tot is this? Where's his mother?
Oh, look at those little cheeks!
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_317: I want one in my stove. No more hauling firewood.
Children, step back, that is no sausage fire!
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_318: A campfire! I'll bake some potatoes.
Not by my wattle fence, it's dry, it'll catch.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_319: If it comes near my gate, it gets the skillet.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_320: Who's digging up there? It's falling on my garden!
Children, away from the edge, it's crumbling!
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_321: Who is that up there? The men thought something up again.
While it is up there, I will take the washing in.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_322: Who left this mess? Your mother taught you better.
Scattered everywhere, like my husband's socks.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_323: That hole is where my cabbages were!
Children, inside! And stay away from the windows!
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_324: Oh, so many cars! How many people ride in there?
If only it stopped once. I would sell my pies.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_326: Keep that thing away from my chickens.
Does it bite? Should I take the kids inside?
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_327: That's it, the kids aren't going outside.
Bolt the doors, shut the shutters. Again.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_328: Finally I can fetch water at night.
Children, play till dark. Today you may.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_329: Not near the nursery! Take that away!
My good dishes are on those shelves!
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_330: Oh, how lovely! Just like at our wedding.
Wake the baby and you'll be rocking him yourself.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_331: That is neighbourly. Bring the plate back clean.
Oh, so rich! I will bring you a pie tomorrow.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_332: Eat, eat, you've gone all skinny.
Here, I baked too much this morning.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_334: Lovely wool! Enough for socks for the whole family.
Give me the wool, I'll knit the kids a blanket.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_335: That wool's going into socks. Thank you, sheep.
She'll freeze, poor thing. Into the barn tonight.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_336: A bit more wool and my husband gets a new sweater.
Good wool. I'll dye it blue, to match my eyes.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_337: There's a boat, but who's got the fishing rod?
I'll sit a while and rest from the kitchen.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_338: Why am I sitting here like in a washtub?
Don't push yet, I'm not holding on.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_339: Ugh, sticky! Go round it, don't track it inside.
It wobbles like my jelly on the table.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_340: You crawl like my husband heading to the garden.
Take my arm, I'll walk you to the bench.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_341: My feet feel stuck in a bucket of clay.
A snail is overtaking me. How shameful.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_342: Since it's sniffing anyway, let it dig my beds.
A Sniffer! If it finds seeds, I'll plant them.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_343: The snowman's here, and the kids are still in summer clothes.
Don't go near my stove, you'll melt.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_344: Oh, you! I just washed this dress!
Right down my collar! You're in trouble now!
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_345: From an egg? And I carried mine nine months!
Oh, a newcomer! Hungry, I bet? Come, I'll feed you.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_346: Who left a fire unwatched? I'm fetching a bucket.
Might as well roast potatoes while it burns.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_347: Work is work, but lunch is on schedule.
Come over, I'm honest, I don't short the scales.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_348: My hem's soaked! Now it's drying by the stove.
Well, at least my feet get washed.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_349: Oh, hold me, I've got buckets!
Someone made a skating rink, and I need the well.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_350: You could bake bread right on this floor.
Oh, my slippers! My new slippers are smoking!
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_351: Oh, so many guests! I only baked enough pie for one.
Are you all related? Your noses look alike.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_352: Those are my husband's beets! Hands off!
Hungry? Ask, and I'll feed you. Don't steal.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_353: Strong, are you? Then fetch me two buckets of water.
I could use arms like that on washing day.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_354: Morning already? The dough hasn't even risen!
I just closed my eyes and the rooster's already crowing.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_355: Night? I haven't brought the washing in!
Children, home! It's getting dark and dinner's not ready.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_356: Mmf! Get me out of this wall!
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_357: Ugh, rotten eggs! Shut the windows!
Just keep it away from my hens.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_358: Sunday. Even I sit down today. Briefly.
Put on a clean shirt, we're visiting my sister.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_359: Is that for jars? I have nowhere for my jam.
Another knick-knack. Where do you even put them all?
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_360: One swing, and my mint got mowed as well.
If weeds fell like that, I would sleep a week.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_361: Quick, are you? Run to the neighbour's for salt.
Running about like my youngest after supper.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_362: If you can make anything, build me a new stove.
Flying! I'd settle for a ladder to the attic.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_363: Ow! My ears! My eyebrows! My pantry!
What was that? I can't hear the kids!
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_364: Take an oven mitt. My hands still bear the marks.
Your furnace is hot. May I set my pie beside it?
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_365: Tamed it? Now feed it and brush it yourself.
Oh, a sweet one. Just no muddy paws in the house.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_366: A pup with a collar. Whose? You feed it, then.
Oh, little paws all over my clean floor.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_367: Someone else's dog, drinking from my bowl.
A fine guard. We could use one by the henhouse.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_368: Oh! I almost dropped my basket of eggs!
I wish I could do that, to market and back.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_369: It hums like a hive. Bees are kinder though.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_370: The eye flew off. I hope it skips my well.
Look, it flew over my garden. Did it crush anything?
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_371: You scatter things like my youngest scatters socks.
Not needed? I will find it a use at home.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_372: Thursday. I bake bread for the whole week.
Thursday already? The beans aren't even picked.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_373: My porridge is on the fire and the day just flew!
What's going on? The shadows are running round the yard.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_374: Heavens, an iron mountain stood up! Hold the children!
If it comes close, I will throw a pot at its back.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_375: It cracks like my old jug. So it will fall apart soon.
Steam pouring out! Step back, you will get scalded!
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_376: I dislike that ringing. I will take the milk off the stove.
They whisper at the forge like sorcerers. Mine stands there too.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_377: The plates are crawling! Feet up, ladies!
I swatted one with my broom. Bring more.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_378: That is it, silent. I am putting the kettle on for everyone.
Hug your family. I have already counted mine.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_379: Asleep, good. Let it sleep like my husband after lunch.
Walk quietly past the forge. Let sleeping trouble lie.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_380: My oven fork cracked just like that. Happens, do not grieve.
Keep the broken bit, it can prop up a garden bed.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_381: My carrots?! I've grown them since spring!
Out of here, or you'll get the broom!
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_382: Let me out! My soup will boil over!
The children will be home soon. Open up!
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_383: I sewed that quilt myself! Put the flint down!
Burn our bed and you answer to me, not the mayor.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_386: No need for a blanket here, the sky's an oven.
How can I sleep here? The pillow's smoking.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_387: Trade? I just sit and count the crows.
Ask my neighbour, she's the clever one.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_388: No job, I stay home, bake and knit.
Give me a workstation first, then we'll talk.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_389: Tuesday. A good day for darning socks.
On Tuesdays my neighbour comes to gossip. I'm ready.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_390: Don't bother her, she's come to lay her eggs.
There's one who always has her house along. I'm jealous.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_391: Hey, iron thing, do not trample my seedlings!
Should I feed it? What do they even eat?
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_392: Not on my shelf, I will not be dusting that.
Pretty little thing. Does it bite?
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_393: Let's walk by the bakery, the news there is fresher than bread.
Slow down, I want to look at the gardens.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_395: Scoot over, let me warm my hands.
Let me tell you how my grandmother outwitted a fox.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_396: Don't rock it, I can't swim.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_397: Spare me a pinch for my cucumbers, they are lazy.
Easy with it, or the flowers will climb into my window.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_398: Pretty. Now dust them every week, mind you.
Leave a spot for my good teacups.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_399: Lovely light. Now nobody on our street can sleep.
With that beam, my husband can't get lost coming home.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_400: I could use a cough potion for my youngest.
You're brewing something that smells worse than my soup.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_401: Just don't let the smoke into my laundry!
A campfire? Good, I'll bring the potatoes.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_402: Mark the market on it, I always get lost.
Draw my garden bigger than the neighbour's.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_403: Don't you dare boil socks in my cauldron.
I bathe the children in that on Saturdays!
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_404: Put my recipe book on the top shelf.
Dust those books first, they've sat there all winter.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_405: Peelings go in there, not my good carrots!
Good. My roses could use some of that.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_406: A box that works by itself? I'd want one for laundry.
It makes things itself, and my husband still hasn't hung that shelf.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_407: Since you're crafting, make me a rolling pin.
Don't drop shavings on the floor, I've swept.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_408: Careful, when it shoots, it goes through the window!
I'd like one to scatter grain for the hens.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_409: Don't slam the door, the baby's asleep!
The hinges squeak, I must ask my husband to oil them.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_410: Drops everything, like my youngest with plates.
If only it dropped things in a basket, not the ground.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_411: That's not how you bake bread, the dough needs to rise.
While it's hot, put my potatoes in too.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_412: Sharpen my knives too, while you're at it.
It shrieks so! The baby will wake again.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_413: My husband and I met to this song.
Turn it up, I do the dishes to this one.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_414: Nice rope. I could hang my washing on that.
Is that how you walk a cow? Show me.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_415: Weave me something for my kitchen window, dear.
My mother wove on one of those. Mind the threads!
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_416: A chest that fits in my apron? I need ten.
Pack the kids' winter things in there, would you?
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_417: Fix my husband's hoe while you're at it.
Shiny armour won't wash the dishes, you know.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_418: Cut me a nice step for my porch, please.
That screech curdles my milk every time.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_419: Oh, my heart dropped! I was already running for towels.
A golden trinket saved you, and I nearly went grey.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_420: I would vanish like that when my husband snores.
Gone, and not even a goodbye.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_421: All that clanging, and the baby just fell asleep!
Could you straighten my bent frying pan too?
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_422: Enchant me a broom that sweeps by itself.
Books turning their own pages. I'll stick to recipes.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_423: A chest my husband can't rummage in? Perfect.
Hide my best jam in there, please.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_424: My husband gave me a flower. A dandelion. Sweet fool.
Looking for a sweetheart? My neighbour's daughter is free.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_425: Oh no! Someone run and fetch the cleric!
Poor soul. Who's going to tell the family?
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_426: They say the smith was talking to a chicken again.
Just between us: the farmer has a new nose.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_427: Who sleeps in iron? You'll tear all my sheets.
At least my husband takes his boots off for bed.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_428: Damp as my cellar down here, only worse.
Who led me down here? I've got lunch to cook!
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_429: Oh, I'm not looking down, not looking.
From up here I can see whose garden is best.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_430: This heat! My dough will rise right out of the bowl.
I need a kerchief on my head, or I'll get sunstroke.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_431: No garden, no neighbours. Deadly dull.
How will I find my way home from here?
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_432: Time to bake gingerbread, or the kids won't let me rest.
I must finish knitting the gift socks in time.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_433: My jam's all jarred, winter can come now.
The kids will gorge on sweets again, and I'll mend their teeth.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_434: You can't even dig a garden bed here, all stone.
So tall, and they can't even say hello.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_435: Laundry would dry here in a minute.
Smells like my neighbour's kitchen when she bakes.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_436: Husband, there's a spider on your back! Joking, April Fools.
Salt in the sugar bowl? I know exactly who did it!
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_437: Set the table, bake the pies, and still dress up!
This new year, I'll teach my husband to do dishes.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_438: Friday means bath night. Husband, are you listening?
The house must be tidy by Friday, guests are coming.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_439: Monday means washing day. The tub's mine again.
Woke them all, fed them all, and it's barely morning.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_440: Saturday is market day! Sell eggs, buy thread.
It's Saturday, and my dough is rising. No rest for me.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_441: The Sunday pie is in the oven, I'm in no hurry.
At least on Sunday my husband stays home.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_442: Thursday's when I bake bread for the whole week.
It's Thursday and my back hasn't straightened since Tuesday.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_443: Tuesday means ironing. Another mountain of shirts.
Washed yesterday, darning today. That's my week.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_444: Midweek and the pantry's already empty.
I promised the neighbour a pie on Wednesday. I forgot!
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_445: It's the weekend, and the kids are up before the rooster.
Everyone gets a weekend except me and the cow.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_446: Good. Then fish my bucket out of the well.
My son will want that too. Don't show him.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_447: So pale! Sit down, I'll pour you some broth.
You need fattening up, you're skin and bones.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_448: I can't even lift a bucket of water now!
Who'll move my barrel of cabbage now?
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_449: What a sight. At least let me sew the patches straight.
My husband dresses better, and he mixes up colours.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_450: With a pack like that you should go to market.
If there is room in there, take my basket along.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_451: All that noise, and my dough will not rise.
Singe my thatched roof and you will rethatch it yourself.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_452: You cannot even fetch water in a suit like that.
Pretty, but how do you sneeze in that thing?
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_454: Half the week gone, and the chores haven't shrunk.
Wednesday is soup day. Hungry? Bring a bowl.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_455: Weekends are for rest. For everyone but mothers.
No work today? Then you can carry my water.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_456: Children, into the cellar! Now, don't look back!
Three heads, all angry. Worse than my mother-in-law.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_457: Children, stay close to me. And no running.
Those soup bones are for the pot, not for you.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_458: A workshop? Just no knocking past nightfall.
Good, at least you will clear the junk from the house.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_459: Taken apart again? I saw who carried planks off at night.
You fix it, I will brew tea. No rush.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.r_w_460: Ugh, it reeks of rot. What kind of guest is this?
Don't look at him and he won't bother us. Probably.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.gmrypkh: I know! I stopped my child growing up. He's stuck this way. Forever.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.wrswgis: Some say that he died that day and that his spirit still haunts the overworld, tethered to those dogs. Only appearing during the day. Still looking for better trades.
Ah. A customer. A legitimate customer! Which of course is all I have.
I pride myself on fair deals. Fair for me, at least. Which usually works out fine for everyone!
I should warn you, I operate a very above board trading system... mostly above board. Some of it is board adjacent.
Welcome, welcome! I've got... let's call them imports from the neighboring villages. Very affordable. Very discreet.
The fire has gone to sleep! Everyone be quiet so it can rest.
You killed the fire! It was so young! It had so many things left to burn!
That's hard Clay! I tried to eat Clay once. I will not be eating this.
You lit the roof — bold and stupid at once. Get off the attic, pyromaniac!
We fixed that roof all winter, thanks a lot.
Now we get drafts… and flames.
Fire on top — new landscape design?
Lava by the house — so cozy, thanks. We are not in the Nether, just saying!
A hot little stream under the window? Nope.
Neighbors asked for a fountain, not hell soup.
Spawn eggs in the village — great plan… for chaos. Put the monsters back in your pocket!
We invited guests, but not these! Move that spawner away from the bell.
Monsters on the square — a festival of fear. Who ordered apocalypse for lunch?
TNT by homes — city planner or demolisher? Take that fuse back where it came from!
Evacuation! Someone wants a wider square… via boom.
Drag the dynamite away from the beds!
A loud landscaping plan, very loud.
Loading the cannon — we are already behind the haystack. At least shout boom as a warning!
A big-gun shot — perfect way to wake the county.
Thanks, the neighbors were not sleeping.
Gun crew has arrived. The village goes on vacation.
Shooting a villager — that is not a trade, that is war! Lower the barrel before the bell rings alarm!
We will open the complaint book… if we survive.
A firearm argument is weak diplomacy.
A gun bench in the village — questionable zoning.
Ammo crates by the bakery. It no longer smells like bread.
An unlicensed armory with attitude. We would prefer a bun shop.
A Create wrench — classic for someone who will just tweak it. Do not tweak our bell!
That wrench makes you look dangerously competent.
Keep it away from my door.
One turn of the wrench and life changes.
A blaze burner — cozy like a hellish fireplace. Do not roast marshmallows over it near kids.
Caged fire stares at me judgmentally.
Farmer's Delight food — civilization on a fork!
Leave a bite for a neighbor, be human.
Smells so good even a nitwit got hungry. Share, do not be shy.
Sharing a hearty meal — the village loves you ten emeralds more. Thanks from belly and soul!
That is diplomacy — through a plate. We are ready to negotiate second helpings.
Food as a peace treaty. We sign with our mouths.
A space suit in the village — stylish and stuffy-looking. How do you breathe? Through a mod?
You look like a moon guest at the fair.
The helmet reflects our curious faces.
A storage terminal — trader envy number one. Show us the free button!
A warehouse in a window. Magic. Dangerous for our business.
Inventory looks endless. Prices do not. Pity.
A waystone — a door without a door. Write the address large, we forgot glasses!
A teleport stone by the well. Tourism classic.
Do not forget the return ticket.
A portal for lazy feet and busy heroes.
We want a home button too.
Enriching fire — sounds like a spa day for ore. For villagers it means stay back.
Strange flame. Even torches are jealous.
Fire that teaches ore to be smarter. It teaches us to run.
An oil pumpjack — the village smells of money and trouble. Do not pour crude into the well!
Black sludge and white shirts are poor friends.
We wear white. Well, we did.
Oil pumps in time with gossip.
Blaze cake — a dessert with fire attitude. Extinguish after the bite!
Tea for us… and a water bucket.
A train schedule — power over time!
If late, blame the rails, not us.
A paper of stops. Village fate in pencil. Write stop at the fair.
The train timetable beats our sleep schedule. We are already awake.
A jetpack in hand — flight starts with oops. Take off away from chickens!
A backpack firework of personal freedom.
Thrust in hand. Calm is not.
TFMG steel — the village feels progress in its spine. Maybe a fence, not a rocket?
An ingot more serious than our council.
Metal for serious work. We nod seriously.
A Sophisticated backpack — a warehouse on shoulders. Careful on turns, you will clip a stall!
So many pockets — and none for conscience?
Joke. Conscience is in the front pocket.
Pockets like floors. We live on the first.
A diamond cannon shell — luxury apocalypse.
Shoot sky fantasies, not the barn.
Shines brighter than our fair. And more dangerous than our elder.
We are poor and intact, thanks.
An unusual blade — the vanilla sword smokes aside.
Do not train on scarecrows without asking!
A weapon with modded attitude. We have attitude too. Peaceful, until you swing at us.
Steel not from our forges. The shine still impresses.
Bone meal — accelerator for gossip and sprouts. The bed thanks you. Neighbors suspect magic.
You sprinkled — and life greened faster than the mayor's report.
May we have a little optimism too?
Fertilizer with attitude. Plants already strut.
The crafting table clicked — a new thingie was born!
Show us, we will make a smart face.
Crafting before the village — engineering theater.
Crafted. We already invented why you need it… joking. Or not.
Into the saddle — dust like gossip! Do not stomp crops at a gallop.
We wave from a safe roadside.
A note-block note — concert without the mayor's permit!
Square music. Pigs thrilled, chickens shocked.
Sounds like the bell tried jazz. Experimentally approved.
Crit! Even the air said ouch. Pretty. Cruel. Effective.
A hit with real flair. We did not ask for flair, but we rate it. Keep going past us.
Critical moment for the fight and our calm.
You are the village shield today.
An animal baby! Village officially melting. We will vote on names.
A newborn fluff. Hearts melted faster than butter.
Herd reinforcement. We do not tax joy.
Shield ready — peace through wood and iron.
We will stand behind you… morally.
The shield says no to hits. We say yes to the hero. Just do not bash neighbors with it.
A map in hand — you are either lost or important.
Show where we are drawn cute.
Paper knows more roads than the mayor.
Do not crease the corner with our village!
Adventure cartography. We are the stable home dot. Return along the line.
Emerald ore — currency of our hearts and prices!
Green shine of economy. Pockets sang.
Discount for villagers? At least a smile.
Ore of deals. We are ready to trade stares. And carrots if needed.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.e06mood: Raising an altar. Do not ask why — ask when.
Dark stone likes silence. And other people's nerves.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.e22mood: Script aborted. Villagers wander off, shrugging it off.
Rehearsal cancelled. Stones stay — drama too.
The tocsin is silent. Trading without knee-shake again.
We survived. Someone even kept their hat.
On the plaque, in italics: survived the tocsin.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.kid_pla: Oh no! You disappeared!
Get up! Come on, get up!
Will you come back? Heroes always come back!
I'll hold onto your stuff while you're gone.
That wasn't a very good idea.
Mom, the hero fell down again!
I'll put a flower on your pillow.
Be more careful next time, okay?
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.w_monst: Oh no! Someone get a pitchfork!
Those zombies again. No peace at all!
Stay back! I have a rolling pin!
Golem, where are you when we need you?
Shoo! Go away, you ugly thing!
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.n_funer: A good villager. A kind neighbour. May the earth rest light on them.
We remember you. And the bell remembers too.
Gone quietly, as they lived. Rest in peace.
Everyone who lived here is part of the village forever.
Let's not grieve too long. They wouldn't have wanted that.
Thank you for everything, old friend.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.n_m_mou: How will we manage without you...
You always knew what to say. I don't.
The Geiger counter clicks like a nervous cricket.
Compliment to the village or a sentence?
Click-click — my new favorite horror soundtrack. Check your boots, they might glow.
The device whispers bad news. We put on a brave face. And step aside.
guide.villager_life.given: You have the Villager Life Guide: open it to learn how villages live, love and celebrate.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.wrjbddm: Ok, so get this... [mumbling] mm-hm, and then...
[shivering] It feels like my nose is about to fall off.
Ow! I can't feel my toes! I don't have any toes!
vnap.mayor.elected: %s is elected mayor of the village
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.s_elect: [clears throat] Thank you, thank you! I won't let you down. Probably.
Mayor! I'm the mayor! Somebody write that down.
I had no job, and now I have an office.
[proud] I promise warm houses, full pantries and fewer creepers.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.s_w_ele: [clears throat] Thank you for your trust! I'll have this place in order in no time.
Mayor? Me? Well, somebody has to keep an eye on you lot.
[proud] First, clean streets. Second, pies at the square.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.s_cheer: Well, at least someone's in charge of the bell now.
I voted for him! I think.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.s_w_che: [cheering] Congratulations! Just don't let it go to your head.
At last there'll be some order in this village!
A mayor! I must bake a cake at once.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.s_stone: A mayor needs a house with a balcony. For speeches, of course.
I lay the first stone! And the rest of them too, it seems.
Here stands the town hall. Well, a big house. With banners!
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.s_w_sto: A mayor needs a proper house. With a porch and flowers.
I'll lay the first stone myself. It's safer that way.
My house goes here. And a balcony, so I can see everyone.
[happy sigh] It's done! The village has a town hall now.
Red banners, a carpet runner... I'm touched.
The doors of the hall are always open. Except at night.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.s_w_hal: [happy sigh] What a house! I won't be ashamed to have guests here.
Flowers by the porch, banners on the wall. Lovely!
The hall is ready. Come in, but wipe your feet.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.s_speec: [clears throat] Citizens! A new day, new emeralds. To work!
Good morning, village! Today nobody teases the golems.
The news: the crops are growing, the bell is ringing, the mayor is awake.
A reminder: shut your doors at night. Especially against zombies.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.s_w_spe: [clears throat] Good morning! Children to school, grown-ups to work.
An announcement: whoever took my watering can, bring it back by lunch.
Today is a fine day for nothing to explode.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.s_answe: Could you say more about the emeralds?
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.s_w_ans: Quite right! I always thought so.
And when will the road to the well be fixed?
[laughing] Oh, our mayor is in fine form today!
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.s_inspe: Right, the walls are straight, the roof is coming. Approved!
A good house going up. One more family, one more vote.
[impressed] You build fast! Perhaps you'll touch up my hall too?
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.s_w_ins: Bigger windows, please. A house should be full of light.
Someone will live here soon. I must drop by with a pie.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.s_prais: Excellent work! The village is proud of you.
It's people like you who hold this village together.
Keep it up. There's no bonus, but thank you.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.s_w_pra: Good work today. Go home, they're waiting for you at supper.
The village would be lost without you. Honestly.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.s_wed.0: [solemn] By the power vested in me by the bell, I now pronounce you husband and wife!
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.s_wed.1: Dear villagers! Today our village has one more family.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.s_wed.2: Love each other and don't quarrel over the pantry.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.s_w_wed: [solemn] By the power vested in me by the bell, I now pronounce you husband and wife!
[sniffing] I always cry at weddings. Love and happiness to you both!
Look after each other. And don't forget to sweep the house.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.s_funer: [sad sigh] The village has lost a good neighbour. We will remember.
Rest in peace. Your house and your work won't be forgotten.
The bell rings softer today. Farewell, friend.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.s_w_fun: [sad sigh] We have gathered to say goodbye. Sleep peacefully.
You were part of our village. And you always will be.
May the earth be soft and the flowers on your grave bright.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.s_resig: [sigh] A mayor without a home is no mayor. I resign.
Let the village choose someone better. Or at least someone with a bed.
I hand back the office. I'll keep the hat, though.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.s_w_res: [sigh] You can't run a village without a roof of your own. I'm stepping down.
Choose a new mayor. And may they be tidier than me.
That's enough speeches for me. I'll go bake a pie instead.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.s_inher: [sigh] Father would have wanted me to look after the village. I won't let him down.
The office came down to me. Along with the hat.
The mayor's family doesn't abandon the village. It's my turn now.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.s_w_inh: [sigh] He did so much for the village. I'll carry on his work.
I'm the mayor now. The family won't leave you unattended.
I saw it all and I remember it all. I'll manage.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.s_noroo: [sigh] There's nowhere for the hall to stand. I'll look again tomorrow.
The village is cramped and the hall is big. I'll wait for some ground to free up.
Not one flat patch of ground! Who built this village?
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.s_w_nor: [sigh] No room for the hall. I'll look again tomorrow.
Everything's taken: houses, gardens, pens. Never mind, we'll wait.
The hall can wait. The village comes first.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.s_clear: This house has stood empty for ages. We'll take it apart, the hall goes here.
Right, beam by beam. An honourable retirement for the old house.
[grunting] An empty house is wasted ground. A hall is not!
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.s_w_cle: Nobody lives in this house. We'll take it apart and build the hall.
A pity about the old house. But the hall is needed more.
Carefully, plank by plank. We'll want those boards.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.s_rebui: [sigh] There's no other place. I'll take my own house down, the hall will stand in its place.
We'll stay with the neighbours for now. A hall afterwards, though!
Goodbye, old house. You were good, but cramped.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.s_w_reb: [sigh] We'll have to take our house down. The hall will stand in its place.
Never mind, we'll manage. The new house will be roomier.
We lived here, and the hall will be here too. That feels right.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.s_offic: The desk here, the shelves there. An office should command respect.
[grunting] Books are heavy. Wisdom always is.
There. Now I can receive visitors here.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.s_w_off: The desk by the window, flowers on the desk. Work should be done somewhere pretty.
The office is nearly done. Just the banner left to hang.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.s_w_set: A rug here, a candle on the night table. Now it's a home.
A town hall is all very well, but children need a cosy home.
[happy sigh] A table by the window, flowers in the corner. Lovely!
tooltip.villager_life.market_counter: The village stall's counter: trade here with the shopkeeper, buy and sell for coins.
tooltip.villager_life.copper_coin: Village money. 64 copper make a silver coin; a full stack changes up on its own.
tooltip.villager_life.silver_coin: Village money: 64 copper. 64 silver make a gold coin.
vnap.shop.closed: The stall is shut: the shopkeeper is away (or it is night)
vnap.shop.refuses: The shopkeeper will not trade with you: the village is angry with you
vnap.shop.no_stall: This counter is no village's stall
vnap.shop.title: %s's stall
vnap.shop.how_to_buy: Click: buy one. Shift-click: a stack
vnap.shop.unwanted: The stall does not deal in that
vnap.shop.till: The till is too low today
vnap.shop.full: The shelf is full of these
Shopkeeper? Me? Well, I can count. Up to ten, at least.
[happy] A stall of my own! I've dreamed of selling bread all my life.
The village has grown, so it needs a stall. And I'll be the one to build it.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.m_w_tak: Shopkeeper! At last someone trusts me with the till.
[happy] A stall of my own! Now we'll get on in life.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.m_lay.0: Right here by the bell, everyone walks past. Perfect.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.m_lay.1: A counter, an awning, a couple of barrels. What could go wrong?
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.m_w_lay: The awning will be striped. Red and white, I've decided.
It's busy here by the bell. I'm building.
Now, where are my planks? The stall won't wait.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.m_noroo: [sigh] Not a scrap of free ground by the bell. I'll look again tomorrow.
Everything's built over! Where do I put the stall, on a roof?
No room. I'll have to trade from my hands for now.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.m_w_nor: [sigh] Not one free corner by the bell. I'll look tomorrow.
It's cramped here. The stall will wait till there's room.
[proud] The stall is open! Bread, candles, beds, come and buy!
Done! The shelves are full and the till jingles.
Welcome to the best stall in the village. Also the only one.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.m_w_ope: [happy] We're open! Come in, we've got everything.
Shelves full, awning up. Time to trade!
The first purchase comes with a smile. The second too, but for money.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.m_greet: Good day! How can I help?
Oh, a customer! Have a look, fresh bread.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.m_w_gre: Hello! What will it be today?
Come in, come in! The very best for you.
I've got candles and pies here. Well, nearly pies.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.m_w_tha: Thank you, dear! Come back soon.
Now that's a purchase! Wear it with joy.
Thank you. The till's happy, and so am I.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.m_soldo: Sold out! The caravan brings more this week.
[sigh] The last one went this morning. Wait for the caravan.
None left. But there will be! Probably.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.m_w_sol: Oh, all gone! The caravan will bring more soon.
Not now. Drop by after the caravan.
[sigh] They bought it all. Couldn't they leave something!
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.m_carav: [happy] The llamas are here! That means candles and bread.
Unload, unload! The shelves are empty.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.m_w_car: The caravan's here! I'll lay it all out now.
Don't haggle, my till isn't bottomless.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.m_refus: I'm not selling you anything. The whole village knows what you did.
[angry] Go away. We trade with friends here.
Closed. For you, forever. Well, for now.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.m_w_ref: [angry] I won't trade with you. Don't even ask.
After everything that happened? No, thanks.
For the likes of you, everything is sold out.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.m_buyba: I'll take it! It goes on the shelf, someone will need it.
Hmm, not bad. Here are your coins.
Deal. Just don't sell it back to me at twice the price.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.m_w_buy: I'll take it. Onto the shelf, and let it wait for an owner.
Here are your coins. A pleasure doing business.
A good thing, a fair price. Agreed!
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.m_buy.0: That's just what I need. I'll take it!
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.m_buy.1: I saved all week. It was worth it.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.m_buy.3: Coins on the counter, the purchase goes home.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.m_w_buy: Bread for the whole family, please.
[happy] This goes in the house. Lovely!
A bit dear, but nothing's too good for the home.
[sigh] Not enough. I'll wait for payday.
Ah, a couple more days of work and I'll buy it.
The prices bite. My purse doesn't.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.m_w_poo: [sigh] Short again. Never mind, I'll save up.
Put that aside for me, will you? I'll pick it up after payday.
The money ran out before the wishes did.
[happy] Coins! Now I can go to the stall.
I worked all day. Every coin counts.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.m_w_pai: Thank you! I'll save it for a new cradle.
[happy] Wages! I'll go and buy bread.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.m_wages: Come for your wages! The village pays for honest work.
[clears throat] The treasury is open. Everyone who worked, come to me.
A coin for everyone. Well, a few each.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.m_w_wag: Wages! Come up one at a time.
[clears throat] The treasury pays. No crowding!
You've earned it, you get it. All fair.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.m_w_hel: The village will help. The treasury will pay.
No family of ours will go hungry.
Take it, take it. Pay it back when you can. Or don't.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.mk_help: The treasury will pay. Nobody in our village goes without bread.
A bed for a child is the whole village's business. I'm paying.
Don't be shy. That's what the treasury is for.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.mk_mats: Planks, stone and glass, please. Lots. A whole wall's worth.
[sigh] Off for materials again. The house won't build itself.
The treasury pays and I carry. Fair enough.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.mk_w_ma: This, this and those planks there. And plenty of them.
You can't raise a wall without materials. I'll take them!
[sigh] Heavy, but it's ours. Off to the site.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.mk_fell: [grunts] A fine log. It'll make planks for a neighbour.
Cut one, plant one. That's what grandpa taught me.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.mk_w_fe: [grunts] It grew well. A pity, but we need planks.
One down, one planted. The farm never stands empty.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.mk_sell: Logs from the farm! Will you take them?
[happy] There's a wage. The harvest goes to the stall, the coins into my pocket.
Fresh, ours, from the village. Pay me fair.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.mk_w_se: I've brought the harvest. Will you weigh it?
[happy] There are coins for the household.
All from our farm. Better than the caravan's.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.mk_arri: Hello! I hear you need a shopkeeper.
I've brought goods and planks for a stall. Where's the bell?
[happy] A village without a stall? I'll fix that.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.mk_w_ar: Hello! Need a shopkeeper? Here I am.
I've brought goods and planks. We'll have a stall up in no time.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.mk_kios: No room for a stall, so I'll trade from a counter by the bell.
This will do for now. A counter means the shop is open.
[sigh] Not a palace, but you can trade here.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.mk_w_ki: The stall wouldn't fit, so the counter goes right by the bell.
Never mind, a counter will do for trading.
[sigh] It's cramped. But everyone walks past.
vnap.shop.budget: The stall has bought enough from you today
vnap.shop.reserved: The rest is kept for the villagers
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.in_w_ro: [softly] Hush now, little one. Mama's right here.
[whisper] Sleep, my sweet. Tomorrow we'll go outside.
Rock-a-bye. Look at those tiny fingers!
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.in_w_hu: Shh, shh, I'm here. I haven't gone anywhere.
[sigh] What is it, little one? Hungry? Just a moment.
[softly] Don't cry, sunshine. Mama's with you.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.in_w_ou: Look who's up on their feet! Off you go, carefully now.
That's the first day behind us. Now I'll have to keep up with you.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.in_visi: Well, hello, little one. It's me, Papa. I thought about you all day.
[whisper] Asleep. So tiny… and so loud.
When you grow up, I'll teach you everything I know.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.in_w_vi: Oh, how sweet! That's his mother's nose, for sure.
[whisper] Shh, asleep. Let's not wake it.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.in_kid_: It's so small! When will it play with me?
Hi, baby! I'm the big one. I'll look after you!
[giggle] It grabbed my finger! Mama, look!
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.in_rock: [softly] Easy, little one. Papa's here. I'm not going anywhere.
Rock-a-bye… Your mother would sing. I'll do what I can.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.in_hush: There, there, don't cry. I'm right here, I won't leave you.
Look at you, up already! Come on, I'll show you the village.
board.villager_life.title: The Town's Notices
board.villager_life.fair: Fair today! The stall pays more
board.villager_life.nothing_wanted: The stall has all it needs.
board.villager_life.how: Bring it here for the full price. Coins in hand go to the treasury.
post.villager_life.yours: This mailbox is yours: villagers' letters will come here
post.villager_life.waiting: You have a letter waiting in your mailbox
post.villager_life.no_box: A villager wrote to you: set up a mailbox to read it
letter.villager_life.thanks_toy: Thank you for the toy you gave %s! It hasn't let go of it since. You are always welcome at our table.
letter.villager_life.thanks_blanket: Thank you for the blanket for little %s. It keeps the baby warm at night — we won't forget it.
letter.villager_life.thanks_match: I don't know how you knew, but %s and I are courting now. Thank you, friend!
letter.villager_life.wedding: %s and %s are getting married today! Come and celebrate with us — the whole village will be there.
letter.villager_life.birth: Good news: little %s was born today! %s is the proudest father in the village. Come and see the baby.
letter.villager_life.funeral: With sadness we tell you that %s has passed away. The funeral is tomorrow morning; come and say goodbye.
letter.villager_life.request: %s posted an errand on the notice board on the square: %s × %s. Whoever brings it is paid well. Thank you!
item.villager_life.house_deed.not_for_sa: Use it inside an empty house the villagers built
item.villager_life.house_deed.bought: The house is yours: %s went to the town's treasury
board.villager_life.lost_hint: Things of yours found on the town's lots wait in the chest by this board.
board.villager_life.lots_hint: Buy a free lot and build there as you like: no villager touches it.
board.villager_life.pick_lot: Click a lot on the map.
board.villager_life.lot_bought: The lot is yours (%s to the treasury). It is fenced now: the way in faces the street, your name is on the sign by it, lanterns at the corners.
board.villager_life.lot_taken: That lot is not for sale any more
board.villager_life.lot_poor: Not enough coins: the lot costs %s
board.villager_life.no_errands: Nobody needs anything brought right now. Errands go up when a household cannot get what it needs.
board.villager_life.errand_hint: Take one errand, bring the thing to the villager and hand it over. Taking another puts this one back.
errand.villager_life.taken: Errand taken: the arrow on the right points the way
errand.villager_life.cancelled: Errand given up: it is back on the board
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.tv_room: A room for the night, landlord! It's been a long road.
[sigh] A roof over my head at last. My feet are humming.
A fine little town. I'll sit here a day or two and look about.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.tv_w_ro: A room, please. One with a window on the square.
[sigh] How far I've walked... At least it's warm here.
What a cosy town. Maybe I'll stay a while.
I'd stay, honest. You just have to talk me into it properly.
A good town. But you don't start out somewhere new empty-handed.
Bring me what I asked for, and I'm your neighbour.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.tv_w_as: I'd stay. But I need a little something to start with.
Talk me into it. It isn't hard, if you know how.
It's lovely here. Bring what I asked, and I'll stay.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.tv_stay: It's settled! I'm staying. Where do you build houses round here?
[laughs] All right, you've talked me round. No more roads!
Thank you, neighbour. I won't let you down.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.tv_w_st: I'm staying! A place of my own at last.
[laughs] You've talked me into it. Time to unpack my bags.
Thank you. I'll be happy here.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.tv_road: Over the mountains, they say, there's a village where everyone's a librarian. How dull!
I was crossing a swamp, and there was a witch... Well, that's a long story.
I saw a desert temple once. Empty inside, and hot outside.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.tv_w_ro: I saw a snowy village. Even the chickens wear fur coats there!
In one town the mayor wore two hats at once. Can you imagine?
The road teaches you one thing: always carry bread.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.tv_rest: Oh, it's good to sit down after work.
[laughs] To our village! And to those who build it.
Best soup around here. Well, the only soup.
They say the caravan comes tomorrow. We'll see.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.tv_w_re: Finally, a seat. On my feet all day.
[laughs] So, tell me, what's new in town?
The tea here is good. Almost like home.
I'll sit a little and then back to work.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.tv_flag: Our town has a flag now! We'll hang it up high.
What colours! It fills me with pride.
A flag over the hall, a flag on the gates. Now that's a town!
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.tv_w_fl: We have our own flag now! We'll hang it by the hall.
Beautiful! Now everyone knows whose town this is.
A flag on the gates, and you can see at once that people live here.
board.villager_life.flag_raised: The town's flag is raised: the villagers will hang it up
board.villager_life.flag_hint: Draw the town's flag: a ground colour and up to three patterns. The villagers hang it by the hall's door, on the gates and by this board.
board.villager_life.flag_hint_up: The flag flies over the town. Draw a new one and the banners already up are repainted.
traveller.villager_life.asks: %s would stay for %s × %s, or %s in coins
traveller.villager_life.no_room: %s would stay, but the town has no room
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.tv_pray: [whisper] It's quiet here. Good to sit and think a while.
[whisper] May the harvest be good and the creepers far away.
[sigh] I'll sit a little. Then back to work.
