subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.spr_ris: [gasp] That was a meadow yesterday. I grazed a cow there yesterday!
The ground hummed all night and the bell rang by itself. Now I see why.
Grew in one night. And it took us three months to put up a house.
The top's broken off and the pieces are hanging in the air. Somebody explain that to me.
The goats haven't calmed down since last night. I wouldn't either, if I were a goat.
[gasp] I was hanging out the washing and there was a tower. I dropped the washing.
It was so bright last night I thought it was a fire. It was stone growing.
Beautiful, isn't it? Only broken at the top, like a pie that sank.
We finished the town, and that same night, this. A coincidence? I don't think so.
They say it's older than all of us. How, if it wasn't there yesterday?
[gasp] A tower! A huge one! Can we go? Please!
It grew in the night while everyone was asleep. The best thing ever, and I missed it!
There are stones flying at the top. By themselves! Honest!
Bet you can see the edge of the world from up there.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.spr_tal: They say every floor inside is a different place. Gardens, ice, workshops. How does it all fit?
The guards in there are stone. Not angry, they say. Just checking who you are.
The smith swears he hears it hum at night. The smith hears a lot of things.
Somebody built it. Long ago. I'd like to shake their hand and ask how they laid the mortar.
People find notes inside. Old ones. As if somebody left them just for us.
The mayor says it's a good sign. The mayor calls everything a good sign except taxes.
My neighbour says there are cherries blooming in there. All year round! I'd like a garden like that.
The shards from in there are warm, like bread from the oven. I held one.
I'm not afraid of that tower. It looks like it's waiting for something.
The men talk of nothing else. They'd do better mending the fence.
They say there's a lantern at the top. Only it's dark. I wonder who put it out.
There are clockwork dogs living in there. They fetch sticks. Really truly!
When I grow up I'm going all the way to the top. And I'll light the lantern.
We're playing spire. I'm the guard and you have to get round me. No, from the side!
Mum won't let me near the spire. She says the spire has its own business.
Bread, check. Lantern, check. Rope, check. Courage… I'll pick some up on the way.
Off to the spire. If anyone asks, I won't be long. If my wife asks, I've already gone.
Time to go. Those floors won't climb themselves.
[sigh] New boots, old legs. Right, let's go.
I'll bring back something beautiful. Or at least bring back myself.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.spr_go_: Supper's in the oven, kids are at the neighbour's. Right, I'm off to the spire.
Somebody has to see those gardens with their own eyes. So I will.
Pack's ready. Checked it twice. Fine, three times.
Don't worry about me. Worry about the guards.
I'll go and gather a few shards. That should cover new curtains.
Well, gate, don't let me down.
[sigh] Deep breath, and in we go.
That tickles! Why does the gate tickle?
See you, town. Don't eat all the pies without me.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.spr_in_: In we go. And no looking back.
Oh, the light's so warm! Like a bathhouse.
I'll be back for supper. Well, the day after tomorrow's.
[laughs] If I'm not back, nobody gets my pie!
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.spr_awa: My wife's up the spire. I'm here with the kids and a cooking pot, and the pot is winning.
She went up two days ago. Every morning I look at the gate.
Mine's on an expedition. Promised to bring back a glowing mushroom. I hope it's not a big one.
She's not home, and the house feels bigger. And quieter.
My husband's up the spire. Went off to be a hero and left me the firewood.
[sigh] He promised two days. This is the third. I'm not worried. Not at all.
He's away, and I still put out three plates. Habit.
Where's mine? Up the spire, where else. Apparently the stone guards beat staying home.
Dad's in the spire! He's fighting stone giants in there. He's probably winning.
Mum went up. She promised to bring me a shell from the glowing water.
When Mum's in the spire, Dad makes porridge. The porridge is… brave.
I wave at the spire every evening. Maybe Dad will see.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.spr_bac: I'm back! Alive, hungry, and full of stories.
The sun! The real one! I missed you.
Somebody pour me some soup and I'll tell you about the gardens up there.
Three days inside, and everything here's just where I left it. A bit insulting, really.
[laughs] My legs are gone and I can't stop grinning. It's good up there!
I'm back! Did anyone feed my hens?
Oh, it smells of smoke and bread. That's what home is.
I saw a hall of ice with lights in the sky above it. You won't believe me.
I'm home. Now I need a bath, a cup of tea and a week of quiet.
Is everyone all right? I'm all right. Good, then.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.spr_tir: [sigh] Back early. The guards had more go in them than I did today.
Brought back two coppers and a bruise. A big bruise, mind you.
The spire won. For now. Give me two days' sleep and I'll show it.
My legs are humming like those walls up there. Don't tell anyone I'm limping.
Not much of a hero. Fine. I'll rest, and I'll go again.
[sigh] Back early. The guards were in a mood today. Now so am I.
A handful of loot. But what blisters! Something to show off, at least.
Don't touch me till tomorrow. I'm asleep. Even if I'm standing up.
Spire two, me nil. Never mind, the game's not over.
An empty pack is lighter to carry. Lucky me, in that at least.
Dad came back and fell asleep in his boots. I'm not taking the boots off, they're scary.
Mum says the spire was stronger today. It'll be weaker tomorrow, right?
Shh! Dad's resting after the spire. He's snoring, so he's fine.
No presents, but Mum's home. That's better than presents.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.spr_fin: [proud] Look what I found! No idea what it is, but it's beautiful.
A Builders' chair! Well, that's what we call it. I'm scared to sit on it, I love looking at it.
Carried it all the way down from the floor. My back hurts, but it was worth it.
This goes in the house. My wife will say 'where', and I'll say 'the corner'. We'll see who wins.
Shards and a few coins. One more trip like this and I'm buying my wife a new shawl.
[happy] Look at this lamp! It was made by people who knew about light.
Found it on the floor with the cherries. It still smells of them.
Nobody touch this! It's for the parlour. Especially not my husband.
Coins, shards and this. What it is I don't know, but it's mine.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.spr_clo: [proud] How do I look? Spire money. I feel like the mayor.
A new coat! The old one stayed on the third floor, with a certain hound.
Don't laugh. This is fashionable. Probably. The tailor said it was.
Fit for a floor of the spire and for a wedding.
[happy] A new dress! Earned it myself, up on the floors.
The colour's like the lights over the ice. The tailor took ages to match it.
Let the neighbours be jealous. Let them get to the third floor first.
Pretty, isn't it? My husband said 'not bad'. That's his highest praise.
Look, I've got new clothes! Dad bought them with spire money!
It's like a real hero's. Only smaller.
Mum said not to get it dirty. That's very hard.
Now I need my own sword. A wooden one. To start with.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.spr_cha: Heard? Our neighbour beat a Keeper! As big as a house, they say.
The spire rang like a bell last night. Somebody's got through another ten floors.
[impressed] A Keeper, one on one. I couldn't even handle a guard.
We'll have to buy our hero a drink at the tavern. On me. Well, partly on me.
They say a new chapter's opened up there. I'd like to know what's in it.
The whole market's talking about it. A Keeper's fallen! Prices haven't, though.
I knew they'd do it. I always know. Well, nearly always.
The spire got taller, did you see? That's because the Keeper fell.
I'll bake our hero a pie. Cherry. They say there are cherries up there.
[gasp] They beat the Keeper! The biggest one! Can I see the trophy?
When I grow up I'll beat Keepers too. Two at once.
Now we're playing Keeper. I'm the Keeper. I fall down really well.
Is it true the Keeper turned into light? Like fireworks?
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.spr_gro: It's grown again! Soon we'll have to tip our heads right back to see the top.
Hear that rumble last night? That was the spire. Rising like dough.
A new tier, a new balcony. It lays stone beautifully, I'll give it that.
The broken top keeps rising. As if the spire's remembering how tall it used to be.
The spire's grown, and my vegetable patch is in the shade again. Never mind, I'll live.
Look how tall it is! Ours must have climbed a long way.
The light in the vein's brighter. Like the spire's heart is beating faster.
Every time I think it can't get any taller. And every time I'm wrong.
The spire's a thousand times taller than me! Yesterday it was nine hundred.
It's growing faster than me. That's not fair.
The flying stones have gone up higher! I count them every morning.
If it grows up to the clouds, can we touch a cloud?
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.spr_bea: [gasp] The lantern's lit! At the very top! You can probably see it a hundred villages away.
The crown's whole. No more break. I don't know why, but I want to cry.
The whole town's in the square. Nobody's sleeping. Who could sleep on a night like this?
They say somewhere far off another lantern blinked back. I believe it.
So many floors. So many boots worn through. And now — light.
[happy sigh] How beautiful. Like the town has finally answered someone.
Such warm light. Like the lamp on the table when you read in the evening.
I'll put a candle in the window. Let the lantern see we're shining too.
We built a town, and the town lit a star. I'll tell my grandchildren.
The lantern's lit! Yellow, yellow! Lots of yellow!
Can we stay up tonight? Please, it's the lantern!
I'm waving at the lantern with both arms. Maybe somebody's up there.
Now other towns can see our spire. Hello, other towns!

spire.villager_life.curio.lectern.1: "Bring more cord. The rope sings when the wind turns."
spire.villager_life.curio.lectern.2: "We counted the steps twice and got two answers."
spire.villager_life.curio.lectern.3: "The Core is warm today. Mason says that means rain."
spire.villager_life.curio.lectern.4: "Do not whistle on the stair. It whistles back."
spire.villager_life.curio.lectern.5: "A room for reading, a room for forgetting, a room for both."
spire.villager_life.curio.lectern.6: "Some of us will not go higher. Some of us must."
spire.villager_life.curio.lectern.7: "The tablets remember what we do not."
spire.villager_life.curio.lectern.8: "Surveyor drew a line the wall refused to follow."
spire.villager_life.curio.lectern.9: "Light the lamps from the top down, never the other way."
spire.villager_life.curio.lectern.10: "The doors open for anyone who asks politely. Ask with your hand."

subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.hro_wat: I walk, I look. While I'm about, you sleep easy.
The sword is heavy, but I'd feel naked without it now.
I've seen worse than zombies up there. Let them try.
I know every fence. Every gate. Every gap in the wall.
[sigh] I used to guard the wheat. Now I guard all of you.
I'm going round the houses. Shout if anything comes, I'm close.
The Builders' armour, and it fits like it was sewn for me.
The children are trailing me again. Let them.
It's scarier up there. Here is home, and I won't let it come to harm.
Sword sharpened, supper in the oven. All as it should be.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.hro_tal: So what's it like up there? Is it true the floors change by themselves?
Thanks for being by the bell last night. I heard you fighting.
Say, is the sword heavy? Can I hold it? No? All right.
My boy says he'll be a hero too. Talk him out of it, will you?
You look just as you did the day you came back. How do you do it?
I've put a pie aside for you. Don't argue, heroes eat too.
Look after yourself up there. We'd be lost without you.
You don't age at all. Share the secret, would you?
My daughter drew you on the fence. With the sword. It's a good likeness.
Thank you for last night. I slept without fear for the first time.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.hro_ans: It's all different up there. But coming back here is the best of it.
Don't mention it. I'd have gone out without the sword, it's just handier with it.
The spire won't let go of me. The years did, though, as you see.
Let him grow. Just have him learn to clean a sword first.
[laughs] You ask me that every day. And every day it's no.
I'll take the pie. Heroes need a crust too.
I do look after myself. But I look after you more.
There's no secret. The spire keeps me in the day I came back.
Tell her my sword is a bit longer. She can draw the rest.
Keep sleeping like that. That's why I walk at night.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.hro_fel: Up there they come in packs. Here, one at a time.
Go back where you came from. Oh, right, you're not going anywhere.
All clear. You can come out.
You can leave the doors open. Almost.
I saw a hundred of these up there. This one was easy.
Done. Somebody clear that off the road.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.hro_tha: [gasp] You got it with one blow! Thank you!
I thought I was done for. Thanks, friend.
That's what we chipped in for your sword for.
Phew. I saw nothing. Well, almost nothing.
A real hero. I'm going to tell my wife.
[gasp] Thank you! My knees went weak.
Just in time! I was walking by with my basket.
You're our angel with a sword.
Come by tonight, I'll feed you. That's not a request.
I'll tell the children. They won't believe it.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.hro_kid: When I grow up I'll be a hero too! With two swords!
[gasp] Did you see that swing? Whoosh!
Can I touch the armour? Just a little?
I practise with a stick too. Every day!
Mum says heroes never get old. Is that true?
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.hro_fal: He stood for us to the last. We won't forget him.
Who'll walk by the bell at night now?
[sigh] The sword goes to the family. The empty place, to us.
Call the mayor. And ring the bell.
He stood between us and it. Like always.
I'll bring flowers. I'll bring them every day.
Who'll tell his children? I can't.
[sobs] He promised to be back for supper.
subtitles.villager_life.dialogue.hro_los: Went up the spire and didn't come back. The gate is silent.
Said he'd go up a couple of floors. A couple of floors...
The spire rarely keeps anyone. But it does.
We'll keep a place for him by the hearth. Just in case.
[sigh] I'll tell the family. Somebody has to.
I waited by the gate till nightfall. No one came out.
The spire is beautiful. I hate it now.
She promised to bring me a pebble from the top.
At least let the chronicle keep her name.
